items.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: put on Louis’ duet record with Earl Hines doing “Weatherbird Rag.” It’s the most amazing thing I’ve ever heard.

ctx.x: Well I think they’re all very good. I think you can teach the basics, the understanding. My biggest problem with most of them is that somebody writes a book and says here are all Charlie Parker’s solos. Once you learn these then you’ll be a jazz player. I mean it doesn’t really work that way. And they don’t really put enough emphasis on listening to people, listening to players that came before. My biggest problem with most jazz education programs is they act like nothing happened before Charlie Parker or Dizzy…
on before that. I mean if you want to hear something innovative put on Louis’ duet record with Earl Hines doing “Weatherbird Rag.” It’s the most amazing thing I’ve ever heard.
And it’s like you said, it came from nothing.
